findings.title: wythoffEdges silently rounds vertex entries beyond 2^53 on a Big board instead of returning them exactly or throwing EngineOverflow
findings.location: packages/engine/src/wythoff.ts:175 (toNumber = Number(arith.toBig(x)), no safety check), used at wythoff.ts:195
findings.claim: On a Big board (any finite board that is not a standard matrix, such as a relabelled type), wythoffEdges converts each bigint vertex entry to a JavaScript number with no check. Entries beyond 2^53 therefore come back as the nearest double. The same input on a SafeInt board throws EngineOverflow, and every other engine conversion of this kind (affine.ts:201, form.ts:74, heaps.ts:109) checks and throws.
findings.expected: SPEC 5.4 lists wythoffEdges as 'exact', and E-1 requires exact integer arithmetic. Oracle: sorted(wythoff_edges([[2,-1],[-3,2]], [2**52+1, 0])) has entries ±13510798882111491 (for example the edge (-4503599627370497, 0) to (4503599627370497, -13510798882111491)). The engine must return those integers exactly or throw EngineOverflow, as it does on SafeInt (E-2).
findings.observed: On fromAdjacency of C = [[2,-1],[-3,2]] (arith Big) with rings [2^52+1, 0], every edge carries 13510798882111492 where the oracle has 13510798882111491. The same rounding appears on relabelled B3 with rings [2^52+1, 3, 0]. No error is thrown. Not reachable from T10, which offers named SafeInt boards and rings up to RING_MAX; it affects the engine API.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus the file: npm ci, then npx vitest run --root packages/engine packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-01-p4-01-wythoff-edges-rounded.test.ts. The test fails with 13510798882111492 against the oracle's 13510798882111491 in six edges. The search harness is packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-01-diff-wythoff-big.test.ts (needs python3).
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 5.4, table 'Geometry', row wythoffEdges: 'exact'; SPEC.md 5.1 E-1 'Exact', E-2 (SafeInt throws EngineOverflow); oracle wythoff_edges (lie_games.py lines 764 to 781); CONTRACTS.md 2.4 wythoffEdges: Enumeration<[number[], number[]]>; decisions/P4-A1.md 'wythoffEdges items, order and truncation' ('entries converted to number') does not say what happens beyond 2^53.
findings.proposedFix: In toNumber, throw EngineOverflow when Number(x) is not a safe integer (or when BigInt(Number(x)) !== x), as affine.ts and form.ts already do; the caller can then retry or refuse.

findings.title: symmetrizer, gram, cartanClass, classify, smallestNonfiniteSubboard and every guarded function throw RangeError on a board with a road count beyond 2^53, where the oracle answers
findings.location: packages/engine/src/classify.ts:105 and :117 (rat(C[i][j]) in symmetrizer), :130 (gram), reaching rational.ts:34 (toBigInt accepts safe integers only)
findings.claim: fromAdjacency accepts any integer road count, and the moves work on the Big board it returns. But symmetrizer builds rationals from entries that are plain numbers, and rat() rejects integers beyond 2^53. So the form functions, cartanClass on an asymmetric board, classify and smallestNonfiniteSubboard throw RangeError 'the numerator ... is not a safe integer'. Every guarded function, through requireFinite and classify, throws RangeError instead of NotFiniteType. Since b85ac0f the symmetric board with the same count is classified (the shortcut skips the rationals), while the asymmetric one is not.
findings.expected: Oracle on C = [[2,-2**53],[-1,2]]: symmetrizer [1, 9007199254740992]; gram [[2,-9007199254740992],[-9007199254740992,18014398509481984]]; cartan_class 'indefinite'; classify [{'nodes': [1, 2], 'kind': 'gcm', 'balanced': True, 'class': 'indefinite', 'name': None}]; smallest_nonfinite_subboard ([1, 2], 'indefinite'). On [[2,-1,0],[-2**54,2,-1],[0,-1,2]]: 'indefinite' and ([1, 2], 'indefinite'). SPEC 5.6: these functions work on gcm boards, and a finite-theory function throws NotFiniteType.
findings.observed: RangeError: the numerator -9007199254740992 is not a safe integer, from symmetrizer, gram, cartanClass, classify, smallestNonfiniteSubboard and coxeterNumber; '... -18014398509481984 ...' on the 3-node board. Links reject such entries, since urlCodec requires safe integers. T16 import calls resolveBoard (which classifies) before its 4-roads check, so its refusal reads 'the numerator ... is not a safe integer' instead of the editor-limit sentence. The cause predates b85ac0f; the symmetric shortcut made it inconsistent.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus the file: npm ci, then npx vitest run --root packages/engine packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-01-p4-02-entries-beyond-2-53.test.ts. 7 tests fail with RangeError and 2 pass (the moves, and the symmetric control).
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 5.6 second table (cartanClass, classify, smallestNonfiniteSubboard, symmetrizer/gram on gcm boards; NotFiniteType for finite-theory functions off the finite types); SPEC 5.1 E-2 ('every other board ... uses Big'), E-11; oracle symmetrizer, gram, cartan_class, classify, smallest_nonfinite_subboard (lie_games.py lines 106 to 126, 1061 to 1077, 1229 to 1271).
findings.proposedFix: Build the rationals of symmetrizer and gram from the board's own entries as bigint (arith.toBig of board.cartan, or BigInt(x) for an integer-valued number) rather than through rat(number).

Oracle docstring, for the owner: averaged_simple_cartan says 'When the board folds by tau this is the transpose of the folded Cartan matrix'. That is false for the identity on a board that is not simply laced: on B2, C2, G2, F4 and B_n/C_n the identity folds to C and the averaged matrix is C, not its transpose (123 cases). SPEC 2.13 states the fact for symmetries of simply laced boards only, where it holds (227/227). Engine and oracle agree everywhere.

geometry.ts says its port is 'operation for operation, so that the floats agree with the oracle's'. The projected points are not bit-identical on 72 of 89 boards, but every invariant agrees within 1e-9. No ring or distinct-point count differs: the closest radius to a 6-decimal rounding boundary is 1.9e-9 away (D12, C11; scratch script ring_risk.py), far above float noise.
